about: Permission patterns /kntl-setup merges into the product repo's .claude/settings.json under permissions.allow and permissions.deny.
Take `common`, one block per platform found, then `mcp`; replace every <server> placeholder with the name from the configured MCP server roster and <owner>/<slug> with the GitHub remote.
Off the list by design: destructive git, `gh api` writes outside this repo's issues, browser clicks and form input, and everything under Owner-only in docs/agents/kntl-conventions.md.

Prefix rules (`Bash(cmd:*)`) end the re-prompting on command variants and match the start of the command only. Deny rules win over allow rules, but a flag placed later slips a deny written for the leading form: `git push origin main --force` passes the `git push` allow and misses the `git push --force` deny, `git branch --delete --force x` misses `git branch -D`. So the allow prefixes below stop at subcommands whose continuations are safe, and on push the per-job İzin paketi stays the second guard; `git-guardrails-claude-code` blocks push at the shell for an owner who wants that.

common.note: `gh api` stays on the list for reads written as `gh api --method GET <path>` and for the wayfinder dependency edge (`gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<slug>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by`); a read by bare path (`gh api repos/<owner>/<slug>/issues/<n> --jq .id`) and every other `gh api` write prompt, and a leading `--method DELETE` / `-X DELETE` is denied. The docker denies cover a remote engine reached by context, host flag, or environment (`docker --context`, `docker compose --context`, `-H` / `--host`, `DOCKER_HOST=`, `DOCKER_CONTEXT=`) and Swarm (`swarm`, `stack`, `service`).

web.note: Local development services (a Postgres container, the app under docker compose) run on the agent's machine. The subcommand-first `docker compose` prefixes reject a leading `--context` or `-H`, and the `common` denies block the context, host-flag, environment, and Swarm forms, so the staging and production runtime stays with the owner.

mcp.note: A bare `mcp__<server>` allows every tool on that server; use it only for servers whose tools search or drive a local runtime (simulator, inspiration). The browser server is listed tool by tool, names as the roster spells them: navigating and reading are allowed; `computer` (clicks, typing, screenshots) and `form_input` keep the prompt, and the İzin paketi covers them per job. Stack half: add the chosen providers' read tools (get, list, search) by exact `mcp__<server>__<tool>` name; provider writes keep the prompt.
